digest.component_or_area: LLM provider integration — Bedrock first-class path
propositions: Rebar lacks a native Bedrock provider path; clients currently front Bedrock through an OpenAI-compatible gateway, losing prompt caching and native structured output.

Bedrock prompt caching is model-dependent and fails silently: us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 caches correctly; us/global opus-4-5 silently omit cache counters while billing full input tokens every call, requiring a warning mechanism.

Some Bedrock model ids reject temperature as a sampling parameter (e.g., us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 returns 400 ValidationException), but pydantic-ai's Bedrock leaf lacks _drop_unsupported_sampling_settings, causing hard failure where the Anthropic path degrades gracefully.

The direct-Anthropic path sets exactly two cache keys (anthropic_cache_instructions, anthropic_cache_tool_definitions); parity requires Bedrock to set the same two, not a third (bedrock_cache_messages).
On-demand model ids are not invokable in the measured account/region; only inference-profile ARNs work, requiring the documented default to be a verified-caching inference profile.

A provider-agnostic error classification rule must translate a 400 bearing a sampling-parameter name and a rejection word into an actionable LLMConfigError naming the model id and both remedies (add to override table or unset config), catching loud failures upstream of silent cost overruns.
